Clean and seal threads. Clean female threads and the face of the shaft prior to installation. Use PTFE (Teflon) pipe tape or pipe sealant on NPT threads. NPT threads should be hand-tight plus 1–3 turns to seal. For parallel threads, use appropriate gaskets or O-rings.

Common mistake: Assuming a 2-passage joint can handle mixed media without verification. If channel A carries compressed air and channel B carries cutting coolant, you need to confirm seal material compatibility for both media — not just one.
Common mistake: Buying a 1.0 MPa joint for an application that runs at 0.9 MPa continuously. Three months later, the seal leaks. The joint did not fail — it was overspecified.
Common mistake: Buying a compact joint with a 3 mm bore to save space, then trying to run a 40 mm bore pneumatic cylinder through it. The cylinder extends slowly or stalls under load.

Common mistake: Selecting a pneumatic rotary joint for coolant without reviewing the wetted materials, seal compound, concentration, temperature, filtration, and cleaning chemistry. Confirm the complete fluid-contact configuration before selection.

Common mistake: Selecting an FKM-sealed joint for a high-speed indexing table without reviewing pressure, speed, temperature, duty cycle, lubrication, and seal suitability. Confirm the combined operating conditions against the selected model and approved specification.

A 1-in-1-out rotary joint carries one medium through one rotating passage. A 2-in-2-out design carries two independent media streams through the same body — oxygen and coolant, for example, or compressed air and vacuum.
